claims.statement: EU rules require initial, periodic or special inspections in defined circumstances, recorded results and evidence of the last inspection when relevant equipment is used outside the undertaking.
Polish labour guidance confirms initial, periodic and special machine controls, but equipment under technical-supervision rules must be inspected by authorized UDT inspectors.
UDT already issues relevant protocols and operating decisions electronically through eUDT, so the candidate can reference but cannot replace the authoritative record.
Ramirent Poland's terms allocate equipment risk to the renter and allow charging repair, parts, labour and certain downtime costs, establishing a real monetary damage-allocation event.
HireCheck already offers the core standalone proposition: timestamped and GPS-tagged photos, customer signatures, inspection history, hire-software integration and one-click damage claim packs.

HireCheck's public first-year Pro price is AUD 79 monthly for up to 100 items, with full price from year two; using the NBP 2026-08-25 rate of 2.6374 PLN per AUD, its implied year-two price is about 417 PLN monthly, far below the original candidate's 1000-3000 PLN for 100 assets.

InTempo, Texada and ToolSense embed inspections, condition photos, signatures, repairs or damage detection into broader rental and equipment workflows, weakening the case for a neutral duplicate ledger.
ToolSense and Trackunit sell broader asset, maintenance, issue and integration platforms on tailored quotes, showing both channel possibilities and incumbent bundling pressure.

Identifiable signatures, user assignments and GPS data require a lawful purpose, minimisation, retention controls and security under GDPR; evidence capture cannot default to unlimited personal-data collection.

The reviewed sources do not establish Polish fleet willingness to buy a separate add-on, channel commitment, admissibility of the assembled evidence in contested claims, or achievable churn and acquisition cost.

contrary_evidence: HireCheck is an exact standalone substitute with public fleet-tier pricing, signatures, GPS, history, integrations and claim packs.
InTempo embeds almost the same inspection evidence into rental software, including timestamps, location tags and customer signatures.
Texada launched AI damage detection inside existing check-out and check-in workflows in March 2026.
ToolSense already supports digital equipment handovers, photos, signatures, maintenance and construction asset records.
UDT's electronic authoritative documents reduce the value of recreating statutory inspection records in a private ledger.
The original 10-30 PLN per-asset monthly pricing is not competitive with HireCheck at a 100-asset fleet.

economics.acquisition_route: Recruit five to ten Polish rental firms using a single compatible rental platform, then seek one integration or reseller agreement only after at least three fleets complete repeated handoff records. The channel hypothesis remains unverified.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Scenario, not forecast: 1000 accounts averaging 500 PLN monthly equals 6 million PLN ARR; at 30% EBITDA and a 4x multiple, enterprise value is 7.2 million PLN and could exceed 5 million PLN of founder equity if the company remains substantially founder-owned and debt-light. Reaching this in 6-8 years requires a scalable channel and low churn, neither of which is evidenced.
economics.founder_time: Three to five hours daily can cover an MVP and a tightly bounded pilot; bespoke integrations, field onboarding, evidence disputes and support would exceed the limit unless handled by a channel partner.
economics.gross_margin_basis: A self-serve SaaS product could target 75-85% contribution margin before channel share, image storage, AI inference, support and claim-review labour. Human adjudication or installation services would materially lower this.
economics.payback: Not established. As a sensitivity, 30 accounts averaging 399 PLN monthly at 75% contribution produce about 8980 PLN monthly before fixed costs, nominally covering 45000 PLN in five months after reaching 30 accounts; time-to-acquire and customer acquisition cost are unknown.
economics.pricing: Test 199 PLN monthly up to 20 assets, 399 PLN up to 100, and 799 PLN unlimited, plus at most 50 PLN for an assembled claim pack. HireCheck's launch pricing is AUD 39, 79 and 149 monthly, doubled after year one; at the 2026-08-25 NBP rate this anchors the 100-item year-two plan near 417 PLN and the unlimited plan near 786 PLN.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every rental cycle can create a custody and condition event, but a standalone product is vulnerable to churn when the fleet's core rental suite adds the same function. Retention requires embedded workflow, Polish document handling and accepted exports.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Localized asset, inspection, handoff, damage, repair and resolution histories can improve exception routing and claim preparation, but only if integrations prevent the system from becoming a duplicate ledger.
fingerprint.customer: Small and mid-sized Polish construction-equipment rental fleets whose current rental system lacks usable mobile condition evidence, Polish inspection-document links or exportable claim packs.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embed through a Polish rental-software integrator, dealer or insurer serving fleets that do not already receive equivalent inspection and claims functions; direct founder-led sales should be limited to a small validation cohort.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: An integration-first evidence add-on joining serial-level statutory-document references, mobile handoff checklists, photos, signatures, repair events and exportable damage claim packs without purporting to certify equipment.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The fleet owner or its rental-software channel pays a flat monthly fleet tier after staff repeatedly complete check-out and return records; an optional fee applies when a claim pack is generated.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Equipment is due for an inspection, changes custody, or returns with alleged new damage that must be documented and allocated before the next rental.

founder_fit: The evidence model, integrations and exception analytics fit the founder's data-science and AI strengths.
A mobile web MVP can be built within 45000 PLN and tested part-time without inventory or field hardware.
The founder can avoid public-facing content, but channel sales, onboarding and integration support may exceed the preferred social load.
Customer configuration and statutory-inspection interpretation must be delegated or standardized so the founder stays within five hours daily.
risks: The product could be a duplicate system of record that yard staff do not consistently use.
Core rental-software and telematics vendors can bundle the workflow and own distribution.
Images and telemetry can show sequence without proving causation, misuse or responsibility.
Incorrectly presenting a private record as a statutory inspection or UDT decision would create legal and safety exposure.
GPS, signatures and worker assignments create privacy, access-control and retention obligations.
Integration and onboarding demands can break the founder's part-time constraint.
Low incumbent pricing makes the original revenue and valuation path unattainable without much larger customer volume or differentiated value.

structure.commercial_archetype: Rental-workflow SaaS add-on and evidence ledger
structure.control_point: The system-of-record integration where each custody and inspection event is written and exported
structure.critical_dependency: A Polish rental channel with customers lacking equivalent features and contractual acceptance of the resulting evidence

thesis: A Poland-localized add-on can link statutory inspection evidence, check-out and return condition, repair and damage allocation for smaller equipment-rental fleets, but it cannot replace competent-person or UDT inspections. Exact and embedded competitors already provide timestamped photos, signatures, GPS, inspection history, claims packs and AI damage detection, so the only plausible wedge is Polish regulatory adapters, data portability and an integration channel at substantially lower pricing than the original per-asset model.
title: Rental Equipment Inspection-to-Claim Ledger
uncertainties: Number of Polish rental fleets whose current software lacks mobile inspection and damage evidence.
Frequency, contested value and recovery rate of damage cases per fleet and asset class.
Whether Polish customers will adopt a separate add-on rather than their incumbent rental suite.
Availability, cost and contractual rights for integrations with the relevant Polish rental systems.
Legal weight of timestamps, GPS, photos and signatures in a disputed damage allocation.
Controller and processor roles, lawful basis, retention period and employee notice for personal and location data.
Channel revenue share, customer acquisition cost, support burden, churn and realized average revenue per account.
